column11: derived: JNJ generated $56,725mm of free cash flow on $263,004mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 21.57% margin, against the 23.4% its filed expense lines leave. Restated before interest: JNJ paid $5,540mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 2.07% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 2.11% to 0.04%. Restated at replacement capex: JNJ spent $13,799mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $8,728mm of depreciation and amortisation less amortisation of intangibles, 1.89% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 0.04% to 0.00%. Restated without one-off cash: JNJ's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $6,000mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,500mm; 2024 instalment 2,000mm; 2025 instalment 2,500mm). None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 27.17% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 31.91%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.74%. It was held at nil, but JNJ books $4,600mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0000200406-26-000016), 4.88% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -4.74%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 JNJ's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,811mm, inventories up $3,901mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $6,344mm, a working capital build of $368mm, 0.14% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -4.74% to -4.88%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.2766 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3207 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -4.4065%.

column11: none of it, and the stage line is why. The Balversa label (DailyMed set id 2a8aa5c0-6c92-4566-8c45-e8f4d1fc20ee, spl version 14, effective 2025-11-17, the row the book's labels table carries) indicates it 'for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) with susceptible FGFR3 genetic alterations whose disease has progressed on or after at least one line of prior systemic therapy'. Both gate studies are the opposite end of the disease and exclude that population outright. MoonRISe-3 (NCT06919965) excludes the 'presence or history of histologically confirmed, muscle-invasive, locally advanced, nonresectable, or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (that is [i.e.], T2, T3, T4, N+, and/or M+)', and MoonRISe-1 (NCT06319820) enrols intermediate-risk Ta low-grade disease with all visible papillary tumour resected. A tumour has invaded beyond the lamina propria or it has not, so in any one year the two pools are disjoint
column12: patients who progress from non-muscle-invasive to metastatic disease are counted once, in the year they are treated. The product sold into this indication is TAR-210, an erdafitinib intravesical delivery system, not the oral tablet the label covers; the book maps both to the Balversa asset, so the layer's price and stopping rate should be checked against the system rather than the tablet before it is built
